past_medical_history: Essential hypertension for 14 years, reasonably controlled
No documented stroke or transient ischaemic attack
family_history: Mother developed dementia at 79 and died at 85; the type was never established
Father died of myocardial infarction at 71

social_history.living_situation: Lives with her husband; independent in all self-care
social_history.alcohol: One glass of wine most days
social_history.driving: Driving without incident; her husband has no concerns

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and fully oriented. MoCA 24/30: loses 1 point on trail-making, 1 on the cube, 1 on serial sevens and 3 on delayed recall (2/5 unaided, 4/5 with cueing). Verbal fluency 13 animals. No aphasia, no apraxia, no neglect.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Visual fields full. Face symmetric. Speech normal.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk, tone and strength throughout. No drift, no tremor.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal base and stride with mildly reduced step length. Tandem gait intact for eight steps. Romberg negative.
neurological_exam.additional: No frontal release signs. No parkinsonian features. Pulse regular at 72.

patient.chief_complaint: Two years of forgetfulness and slowing that she has noticed herself and her husband has not
patient.history_present_illness: Dr. Anna Beltrami is a 69-year-old retired pharmacist who presents on her own initiative with two years of cognitive complaints. She reports that she has to write things down where she never used to, that she has twice arrived at the supermarket without her list and been unable to reconstruct it, and that reading a novel now takes her twice as long because she loses the thread. She has stopped doing the crossword she completed daily for thirty years. Her husband, present at the consultation, does not share her concern: he says she runs the house as she always has, that she has never missed an appointment or a payment, and that he would not have brought her. She remains independent in every instrumental activity, drives without incident, and manages the household finances. She is not depressed; she is worried, because her mother developed dementia at 79. She has had hypertension for fourteen years, reasonably controlled, and takes a statin. There have been no discrete neurological events, no gait change, no falls, no hallucinations, no fluctuation and no dream enactment. Her account and her husband's differ, and both are given without exaggeration.

findings.type: White matter hyperintensity of presumed vascular origin

signal_characteristics.T2_FLAIR: Confluent caps with beginning confluence of deep foci — greater than expected for 69 years but not confluent throughout

findings.location: Mild, symmetric; medial temporal lobes borderline

signal_characteristics.Coronal_T1: Hippocampal volumes at the lower limit of normal for age, symmetric

volumetrics.medial_temporal_atrophy: Scheltens MTA grade 1 bilaterally — within the age-adjusted range at 69

additional_observations: The white matter burden is greater than expected for age but does not reach the confluent Fazekas 3 threshold at which small-vessel disease is held to explain a dementia by itself
One lacune only; SWI shows no microbleeds and no cortical superficial siderosis
Medial temporal atrophy is grade 1 and symmetric — not an Alzheimer pattern
mri.impression: Moderate cerebral small-vessel disease: Fazekas 2 white matter hyperintensity with one lacune and mildly enlarged perivascular spaces, medial temporal lobes within the age-adjusted range. The burden is sufficient to explain mild cognitive impairment but is below the threshold at which small-vessel disease alone accounts for a dementia — which matches a patient who is still functionally independent.

labs.interpretation: LDL 112 mg/dL is above target for a patient with imaging evidence of cerebral small-vessel disease. B12 296 pg/mL is normal but at the lower end. TSH, folate, RPR and HIV are normal or negative. There is no reversible cause for the cognitive complaint.

csf.interpretation: Normal Alzheimer biomarker profile: Abeta42 702 pg/mL, Abeta42/40 ratio 0.081 and phospho-tau 38 pg/mL are all normal, making amyloid and tau pathology unlikely. The cognitive complaint is therefore not attributable to Alzheimer's disease, and the mild deficit is best explained by the documented small-vessel disease.

quantitative_data.pattern: mild executive/processing-speed, memory within normal limits

specialized_test.impression: Mild impairment confined to executive function and processing speed, with memory, naming and recognition within normal limits and normal informant-rated function. This meets criteria for mild vascular cognitive impairment and not for a major (dementia-level) disorder. Serial reassessment is the appropriate management.

clinical_assessment.impression: MoCA 24/30 in a university-educated pharmacist, which for this baseline is a meaningful fall, with an executive and retrieval pattern. Crucially, the informant-rated functional scale is normal at 2/30 and instrumental independence is intact: this is mild vascular cognitive impairment, not vascular dementia, and the distinction determines both the label and the follow-up.

findings.result: Mildly reduced step length, normal clearance
Speed falls 12% while counting backwards — within normal limits

output.impression: Timed-up-and-go 11.8 s, within normal limits, with only mildly reduced step length and normal dual-task performance. There is no higher-level gait disorder, which is consistent with a small-vessel burden that has not yet produced a clinical syndrome.

background.posterior_dominant_rhythm: 9 Hz, symmetric, reactive to eye opening

eeg.impression: Normal awake EEG for age. No epileptiform discharges and no focal or generalised slowing.

labs.interpretation: The additional panels requested are negative and do not contribute to the diagnosis in this presentation.

findings.signal: study performed and reported as non-contributory
findings.description: no finding relevant to this presentation

advanced_imaging.impression: The study was performed and does not contribute to the diagnosis in this presentation.

additional_observations: Chronic ischaemic white matter change, better characterised on the MRI already obtained
ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No haemorrhage, mass or hydrocephalus. CT cannot exclude microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis.

findings: No intracardiac thrombus, vegetation or shunt. No pericardial effusion.
No atrial fibrillation. No pauses. No AV block.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.query: vascular cognitive impairment diagnostic criteria and secondary prevention

results.title: Diagnostic criteria for vascular cognitive disorders: a VASCOG statement
results.authors: Sachdev P, Kalaria R, O'Brien J, et al.
results.summary: Requires a cognitive syndrome documented on a validated instrument plus imaging or temporal evidence that cerebrovascular disease accounts for it.

results.title: Neuroimaging standards for research into small vessel disease (STRIVE-2)
results.authors: Duering M, Biessels GJ, Brodtmann A, et al.
results.summary: Defines and standardises the reporting of white matter hyperintensity, lacunes, microbleeds, perivascular spaces and cortical superficial siderosis.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for vascular cognitive impairment; management is control of the vascular risk factors, secondary prevention matched to the mechanism, review of the anticholinergic burden, and treatment of coexisting Alzheimer pathology where biomarkers support it.

medication_review.proposed: review of the current medication list for anticholinergic burden
warnings: Anticholinergic load is a reversible contributor to cognitive impairment in this population and should be quantified before any new prescription.
medication_review.summary: No prohibitive interaction identified within the current list.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Mild vascular cognitive impairment (mild vascular cognitive disorder) due to moderate cerebral small-vessel disease — the threshold for vascular dementia is not met

differential.key_features: The mechanism is the same and the imaging supports a vascular attribution, but instrumental independence is preserved and the informant-rated functional scale is normal at 2/30, so the major (dementia) threshold is not met and labelling it as such would be wrong

differential.diagnosis: Mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer's disease
differential.key_features: The family history and the amnestic complaint raise it, but CSF Abeta42, the Abeta42/40 ratio and phospho-tau are all normal and the hippocampi are age-appropriate

differential.diagnosis: Subjective cognitive decline without objective impairment
differential.key_features: There is objective impairment on formal testing at the 16th-22nd percentile in executive domains, so the complaint is not purely subjective
Geriatric Depression Scale 3/15 and passed performance-validity measures
The executive scores are below the normal range for her age and education, and she has abandoned a lifelong daily activity

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a collateral history from an informant who sees the patient daily: the shape of the decline (abrupt, stepwise or gradual), whether any step can be dated to a cerebrovascular event, and which instrumental activities have been lost
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Two years of subjective and partly objective cognitive decline with instrumental independence preserved and no informant corroboration of functional loss — the ambiguity that must be resolved rather than assumed either way

optimal_actions.action: Perform a validated bedside cognitive assessment and record the per-domain profile and whether delayed recall improves with cueing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: MoCA 24/30 with a mild executive and retrieval pattern but a normal informant-rated functional scale — impairment without loss of independence, which does not meet the threshold for dementia

optimal_actions.action: Order the reversible-cause screen and the vascular-risk assays that will be treated (CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, RPR, HIV, HbA1c, lipid panel)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Reversible causes excluded; LDL 112 mg/dL above target for a patient with imaging evidence of small-vessel disease

optimal_actions.action: Perform timed gait and balance testing: the short-stepped, wide-based gait with preserved arm swing is part of the subcortical syndrome and separates it from the gait of normal pressure hydrocephalus and of parkinsonian disorders
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Timed-up-and-go 11.8 s with normal dual-task performance — no higher-level gait disorder despite the imaging burden

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI reported in STRIVE-2 terms — FLAIR for white matter hyperintensity with a Fazekas grade, T1/T2 for lacunes, DWI to establish that the lesions are chronic, and SWI for microbleeds and cortical superficial siderosis — together with the medial temporal atrophy grade
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Fazekas 2 white matter hyperintensity with one lacune and age-appropriate medial temporal lobes — a burden that explains mild impairment but not a dementia

optimal_actions.action: Order formal multi-domain neuropsychological testing to settle the executive-versus-amnestic attribution and to document a baseline for follow-up
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Mild executive and processing-speed impairment with preserved memory storage and normal functional scales — mild vascular cognitive impairment rather than dementia

optimal_actions.action: Sample CSF for Alzheimer biomarkers: the question is not which dementia but whether Alzheimer pathology coexists with the vascular burden, because the answer changes what is treated
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Abeta42 and the Abeta42/40 ratio normal with normal phospho-tau — Alzheimer biology is not present, which resolves the ambiguity created by a family history and a mildly amnestic complaint

optimal_actions.action: Confirm the diagnostic criteria applied and the current secondary-prevention targets against the guidelines
optimal_actions.expected_finding: VASCOG 2014 criteria and the 2021 AHA/ASA secondary prevention targets confirmed

optimal_actions.action: Review the medication list for anticholinergic burden and for the interaction between antithrombotic choice and the microbleed burden before prescribing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Anticholinergic contributors identified and the antithrombotic choice reconciled with the imaging burden

optimal_actions.action: Treat the vascular substrate to prevent conversion — intensify the statin to reach an LDL below 70 mg/dL and maintain the systolic blood pressure below 130 mmHg — encourage physical activity and vascular risk-factor adherence, and arrange structured cognitive and functional reassessment at 12 months rather than assigning a dementia label now
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Vascular risk factors treated to prevent progression, the diagnosis correctly staged as mild rather than major, and a reassessment interval set

optimal_actions.action: Disclose the diagnosis and its mechanism to the patient and the informant, and address driving, medication management, finances, advance care planning and caregiver support
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Patient and informant engaged in care planning; safety domains addressed

useless_tools.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome
The MRI already obtained answers everything a CT could and more: CT cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so it cannot grade the vascular burden this diagnosis rests on
There is no embolic lesion pattern to explain: the burden here is small-vessel, and a structural cardioembolic source would not account for it
Prolonged rhythm monitoring is for an unexplained embolic infarct pattern; in pure small-vessel disease it changes nothing about the diagnosis or the treatment

sequence_constraints.reason: Document the cognitive deficit before attributing it: imaging read without a cognitive profile invites over-attribution of incidental white matter change

critical_actions: Establish whether instrumental independence is lost, because that is what separates mild vascular cognitive impairment from vascular dementia
Obtain an informant-rated functional scale rather than relying on the clinical impression
Document the cognitive profile formally when the screen is borderline
Obtain MRI and judge whether the vascular burden reaches the threshold for attributing a dementia
Resolve the Alzheimer question with a biomarker where the family history and the complaint make it live
Treat the vascular risk factors, which is the intervention that reduces conversion, and set a reassessment interval
contraindicated_actions: Do not diagnose dementia in a patient who remains independent in all instrumental activities
Do not start a cholinesterase inhibitor: it is not indicated in mild vascular cognitive impairment and there is no Alzheimer biology
Do not dismiss the complaint as subjective when formal testing shows objective executive impairment
Do not attribute the impairment to a Fazekas 2 burden and stop there without addressing the modifiable risk factors
Do not discourage driving in the absence of any objective driving-relevant deficit or informant concern
key_reasoning_points: Severity staging is a diagnosis, not a formality: mild and major vascular cognitive disorder are separated by loss of independence in instrumental activities, and the informant-rated scale is the instrument that decides it
A Fazekas 2 burden supports a vascular attribution for mild impairment but falls short of the confluent burden required to attribute a dementia to small-vessel disease alone
A discrepancy between patient and informant is information, not noise: a concerned patient with an unconcerned informant and a normal functional scale points to the mild end
Where a family history and an amnestic complaint keep Alzheimer's disease live, a normal biomarker profile settles it more cheaply and definitively than serial imaging
The actionable output in mild vascular cognitive impairment is risk-factor control plus a reassessment interval, since that is what changes the probability of conversion

red_herrings.data_point: A mother who developed dementia at 79
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the assessment on Alzheimer's disease and invites a cholinesterase inhibitor
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Late-onset dementia in one parent confers modest risk, the type was never established, and the CSF biomarker profile here is normal

red_herrings.data_point: Fazekas 2 white matter change on the MRI report
red_herrings.intended_effect: Read as sufficient to diagnose vascular dementia in a patient with cognitive complaints
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A Fazekas 2 burden with one lacune explains mild impairment; attributing a dementia to small-vessel disease requires a confluent burden, and in any case this patient has not lost functional independence

key_educational_points: Mild and major vascular cognitive disorder are distinguished by functional independence, measured with an informant scale
Imaging burden must be matched to the severity of the syndrome before a dementia is attributed to it
A normal Alzheimer biomarker profile is the efficient way to close a differential kept open by family history
Risk-factor control plus a reassessment interval is the correct output at the mild stage
